title: Seodaemun Prison History Hall
description: A modern prison built in 1908 by the Japanese colonial government as 'Gyeongseong Prison' at the foot of Inwangsan Mountain in Seodaemun, Seoul. During the Japanese colonial period, many independence activists were imprisoned here and suffered severe torture and oppression. After the March 1st Movement in 1919, many patriots including Yu Gwan-sun were imprisoned and endured hardships here.

title: Independence Gate
description: A monumental stone arch gate completed on November 20, 1897, promoted by the Independence Club to strengthen their will for independence. It was built after demolishing the Yeongeunmun Gate, which symbolically represented Joseon's tributary relationship with Qing China, declaring complete sovereignty as an independent nation free from the Chinese-centered worldview.

title: Seodaemun Independence Park
description: A historic park opened on August 15, 1992, to commemorate the 47th anniversary of Liberation Day. This site was originally where Seodaemun Prison stood, where numerous independence activists were imprisoned and suffered during the Japanese colonial period. The park was created to remember this painful history and honor the noble sacrifice and fighting spirit of independence activists.

title: Bongwon Temple
description: A thousand-year-old temple reportedly founded by National Master Doseon in the 3rd year of Queen Jinseong of Silla (889 AD), originally called Banyasa Temple. When it moved to the current location at the foot of Ansan Mountain in the 24th year of King Yeongjo (1748), it received the temple name 'Bongwonsa' and a royal calligraphy plaque directly from King Yeongjo.

title: Yonsei University Sinchon Campus
description: One of the pioneers of modern higher education in Korea, originating from Yonhi College established in 1915 by American Presbyterian missionary Horace Grant Underwood and Severance Medical College established by Canadian missionary Oliver R. Avison. This is also the site where Lee Han-yeol died tragically after being hit by a police tear gas canister during the June 1987 Democracy Movement.

title: Ewha Womans University
description: Founded as 'Ewha Haktang' in 1886 by American Methodist missionary Mary F. Scranton, who started with just one student in her home in Jung-dong, Seoul. The name 'Ewha' was bestowed by Emperor Gojong, meaning 'to bear pure, beautiful, and fragrant fruit like pear blossoms.'
